test_policy.notes: Davenport's high school page says it will continue to waive the ACT/SAT requirement for admission; first-time students need an official high school transcript with a minimum 2.0 GPA (catalog). The international catalog line reads 'Diploma or Transcript with 2.0+ GPA on 4.0 scale AND applicable test score'; the test there appears to refer to the English proficiency options (ACT/SAT English scores are among them). SAT 1160 / ACT 24 with a 3.5 GPA is needed only for the Nursing high school direct-admit option.

requirements.notes: Apply through Davenport's own online application. The high school page calls the application 'free'; an international-specific fee is not stated on the pages read, so no fee is shown. International applicants need official transcripts (course-by-course evaluation from a NACES member for schools outside the US/Canada), a signed financial support form, a bank letter or statement issued within 9 months of the intended start, a passport photo page copy, and English proof. Admission is reviewed on a rolling basis.

deadlines.label: International applicants outside the U.S. needing an F-1 visa: complete admission file (fall 2027 entry)
deadlines.notes: Davenport's international deadlines page lists Fall Semester (2027) June 21, 2027 for students outside the U.S. who need an F-1 visa (Winter 2027 is Nov. 2, 2026). Students transferring from a U.S. institution (and Canadian citizens) have August 2, 2027. The page does not say whether it covers undergraduate programs only. Domestic admission is rolling with no fixed deadline.

english_policy.waiver_notes: Test results must be within the last 2 years. Alternatives or waivers: citizens or graduates of waiver countries where English is the official language; U.S. high school graduation; transferable college English and math credits; ACT 18+ Reading and English; SAT 450+ Evidence-Based Reading and Writing; AP English Language 3+; IB English 5; successful completion of ELS Language Centers Level 112 (an ESL pathway).

english.notes: 2026-27 undergraduate catalog. Graduate programs require higher scores (TOEFL 79).

cost.notes: Davenport's 2026-27 undergraduate budget (30 credits, 8 months, dependent on-campus column): tuition and fees $32,945 combined, food and housing $14,280, books and supplies $780, personal $3,008 (transportation $944 and loan fees $66 are not included in other), total $52,023. Per-credit tuition is $1,059 on the first rate listed and $1,148 on a second block that names the Great Lakes Bay, Lansing and Warren campuses; the Grand Rapids rate was not confirmed. Tuition is the same for international students on the pages read

aid.notes: The international page says merit-based scholarships of up to $10,000 per year may be available. The scholarships page lists Executive $10,000/yr (3.85+ GPA), Distinction $9,000 (3.50-3.84), Momentum $7,000 (3.0-3.49), Impact $6,000 (2.75-2.99) and Signature $5,000 (below 2.75); it does not say these are specific to international students, and it lists no international-only awards. Federal and state aid are not available to international students.

majors.program: Business (BBA, D.W. Maine College of Business)
majors.notes: Majors include Finance, Human Resource Management, Management, Marketing and Operations and Supply Chain Management; no separate admission criteria are published beyond general admission.

majors.program: Computer Science and Cyber Defense (BS, College of Technology)
majors.notes: No separate admission criteria are published beyond general admission. Davenport is a National Center of Academic Excellence in Cyber Defense Education.

Admission to the university is not admission to Nursing. High school direct admit: seniors with 3.5+ GPA and SAT 1160+/ACT 24+ (limited seats). Standard admission: 3.0+ GPA strongly recommended, TEAS exam and an essay. Students may take up to 33 credits as undeclared pre-nursing.
